title: usage-signals-breakdown-wireframe-notes
body:
Purpose
This note collects exploratory wireframes, UX constraints, and a prioritized backlog for a console page we are calling "Usage Signals: per-key & per-route breakdowns." The goal: let engineers and SREs quickly answer questions like: which API keys are approaching hard quotas, which routes are seeing transient spikes, who is getting throttled and why, and how billing aligns to API surface area.

Design goals & guiding principles
- Fast triage: single-screen investigation for first-pass analysis (heatmap + last-100 requests table + histogram + alerting suggestions).
- Actionable context: every throttled/failed row points to suggested next steps (revoke key, add quota, mute alerts, route fallback).
- Billing alignment: show tokens burned split by route/model and by plan so product teams can map to invoices.
- Privacy & security: by default mask caller emails and only show full identity to owners/ops roles.
- Lightweight: default view loads in <500ms for tenants with up to 500 active keys.

Primary user journeys we must support
1) Investigate throttles: user sees spike in 429s, filters to last 6h, drills into top offending key, inspects last 50 requests to identify pattern (large batch, long prompts, bursty seq lengths).
2) Quota planning: product manager sees 3 keys near soft quota and asks to increase reserved capacity — needs per-route historical percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and cost projection for 30/60/90 days.
3) Abuse detection: SRE spots a new high-rate key, wants to quickly link to signup email, last known IP region, and optionally rotate the key or throttle with custom policy.
4) Billing reconciliation: finance wants to see a CSV with per-route token counts broken down by plan (self-serve export).

Wireframe (text sketch)
- Header: Tenant selector | Date range (quick presets: 1h/6h/24h/7d/30d) | Key search (id/email/label) | Route toggle (paths with counts)
- Left column (narrow, ~260px): Key list (sortable by tokens, errors, throttles) with small sparkline and current quota usage pill (soft% / hard%). Clicking selects a key and shows its context in main canvas.
- Main canvas (split vertically):
  • Top row: Overview cards (Total tokens, Active keys, 429 rate, Mean latency, Cost estimate for range). Each card has a micro CTA (e.g., "Export top callers", "Create alert").
  • Middle row: Composite timeline (stacked area) showing tokens by route color-coded, overlaid with event markers for quota breaches and deployed rollouts. Hover shows per-route tooltip and token delta between adjacent buckets.
  • Right of timeline: Per-route breakdown table (route, tokens, 429s, avg latency, top keys by token%). Each route row can expand to show sample requests (anonymized) and last 3 models used.
  • Bottom: Recent requests table (paginated, searchable). Columns: time, request_id (click opens trace), key_id (masked), route, model, prompt_len_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, latency_ms, status_code, action_suggestion. Row expansion shows raw headers (redacted) + full truncated prompt + related trace link.

Investigative affordances (detailed)
- Quick filters: token length bucket (short/medium/long), burstiness (requests/min), route type (generate/embeddings/chat), model class (Llama-family, Falcon-40B, tiny).
- Smart grouping: automatically group requests that appear to come from the same client session (same KV cache id or same first 1k chars of prompt signature) to surface noisy intra-key spikes.
- Attribution: show percent of tokens that are user-visible vs system tokens for chat-based routes (helps map to cost).
- Causal markers: annotate timeline with release tags (from CI/CD) and autoscaling events (scale-up/down) to help correlate infra changes with usage anomalies.

Accessibility & permission model notes
- Masking: default mask for key owner email and IPs; admin role can unmask.
- Rate-limit visibility: only show per-key historical rate curves to org admins and security. Product-level aggregated views are available to plan owners without key-level details.

Edge cases and performance considerations
- High-cardinality tenants: for tenants with thousands of keys, render left column as virtualized list and default to showing keys with >1% tokens or >5 errors in range. Add a lightweight sampling mode for timelines (p99 accuracy) with disclosure to users.
- Long time ranges: downsample timelines and compute approximate percentiles. Provide "recompute exactly" CTA that queues a job if user needs exact historical numbers.
- Live traffic: streaming tail view for live troubleshooting that auto-refreshes and keeps cursor position unless user pins a row.

Backlog (prioritized)
P0 (MVP)
- Timeline with stacked tokens-by-route + drill to per-route table (2 wks)
- Recent requests table with trace link and expand (2 wks)
- Left key list with quota pills and quick-sort (1 wk)
- Create basic alert from route or key (threshold or % increase) (1 wk)

P1
- Billing export: CSV with per-route token breakdown by plan (3 wks)
- Smart grouping/session detection (3 wks)
- Masking/permission enforcement UI (1 wk)

P2
- Release/scale event overlay from CI/CD and autoscaler (2 wks)
- Sampling mode for large tenants + prompt-signature clustering (3 wks)
- Suggested throttling policies generator (ML-assisted) (4 wks)

Acceptance criteria (for MVP items)
- Timeline renders within 500ms for footprint <=500 active keys and 24h range.
- Recent requests table returns first page in <300ms for typical tenants.
- Quota pill shows correct soft%/hard% computed from contract data.
- Exported CSV matches totals shown in UI within delta <0.5% for 24h ranges.

Open questions (needs decisions)
- Soft vs hard quota semantics: should soft quota be purely advisory or block writes when exceeded? Product has leaned advisory but security wants stricter control for some plans. Need policy matrix.
- Alert ownership model: who gets alert by default when per-key spike occurs? Key creator, org admins, or billing owner?
- Retention/compute cost: what default retention (30d) do we offer for per-request detail before archiving? Should we tier retention as paid addon?

Follow-ups / immediate next steps
- Sync with SRE (Raj) and Billing (Olivia) to agree on data contract (fields required in recent requests export) — scheduled 2025-01-16.
- Prototype sketch in Figma (Diego) with the left-list/main-canvas split and timeline interactions — due 2025-01-22.
- Wire up a tiny backend mock that returns stacked token time-series + 100 sample requests for demo — eng spike (1 engineer, 1 week).

Notes-to-self (informal)
- Keep the "action_suggestion" column small and opinionated: only 3 suggestions max. Avoid overwhelming users with too many possible remediations.
- Consider a "why am I seeing this" microcopy linked to a KB doc explaining batching/caching/kv-cache behavior for customers.
- When in doubt about privacy, default to more masking.

Conversation pointers (to paste into Slack thread)
- TL;DR: single console page for per-key/per-route investigation + exports. MVP = timeline + recent requests table + key list + basic alerts. Need decisions on soft vs hard semantics and alert ownership.

Example quick scenarios to validate in prototype testing
- Spike due to 1 customer sending a 10k token prompt loop — identify via prompt_len_tokens and suggest batching or rate limit.
- Sudden 429 burst after rollout — overlay release marker and suggest fallback to smaller model.
- Billing discrepancy: tokens in UI vs invoice — add a reconcile button that shows token computation breakdown.

End of notes.
